notes.pattern: NとはNです / Nの意味 / Nを調べます

notes.title: Word usage
notes.pattern: Nという名詞 / Vという動詞

lessons.title: Naming adjectives and adverbs

notes.title: Word usage
notes.pattern: 赤いという形容詞 / ゆっくりという副詞
notes.explanation: Here 形容詞 names an い-adjective such as 赤い. Words that use な before a noun follow a different pattern. 副詞 means adverb, such as ゆっくり. An adverb can add information about how something happens; some adverbs also modify a description or the whole sentence. These labels describe patterns you have already practiced.

lessons.title: Recognizing a familiar way to say you

notes.title: Word usage
notes.explanation: 君, read きみ, is a familiar “you.” You may hear it between close friends or from someone addressing a person of equal or lower status; it can sound condescending in the wrong relationship. These are quotations from a close classmate who habitually uses 君 with the listener. Recognize that relationship rather than using 君 with everyone. A name with さん, or leaving out an obvious “you,” is often a better choice. This is not the name suffix くん.

notes.title: Word usage
notes.pattern: 私という代名詞 / 名前の代わりに

lessons.title: Translation and interpreting

notes.title: Word usage
notes.pattern: NをNに訳します / Nと解釈します
notes.explanation: 通訳 is spoken interpreting or an interpreter. 訳す means translate; を marks the original and に the language of the result. 英文 is English text or an English sentence. 解釈 is an interpretation of meaning. 同意 is agreement or consent. Nと解釈する means understand something as N; an interpretation should not be confused with a direct quotation.

lessons.title: Writing a work and referring to its writer

notes.title: Word usage
notes.pattern: 本を著します / 執筆しています / 筆者の意見
notes.explanation: 著す means author a work such as a book; it is more specific than ordinary 書く. 執筆 refers to writing a text, often for publication. 筆者 identifies the writer of the text being discussed; an author may also use it to refer to themself. These examples distinguish the work, the writing activity and the person behind a passage.

lessons.title: Literature, classics and writing style

notes.title: Word usage
notes.pattern: 文芸の活動に参加します / 文体が違います
notes.explanation: 文芸 refers to literature as an art, including poetry and fiction. 古典 is an established classic, often from an earlier period. 文体 is how a text is written, including its choice of words and sentence patterns; it is different from the story’s subject.

lessons.title: Drafts and publication

notes.title: Word usage
notes.pattern: 原稿を書きます / 本を刊行します / 雑誌に掲載します
notes.explanation: 原稿 is the text prepared for a publication or speech. 刊行 is publishing a book, magazine or similar complete publication. 掲載 is including an item such as an article, photograph or poem in a newspaper, magazine or other publication. The thing being published determines which word fits.

lessons.title: Words for books and written works

notes.title: Word usage
notes.pattern: 図書 / 書物 / 書籍
notes.explanation: All three words can refer to books. 図書 is common in library and institutional contexts. 書物 emphasizes a written work and often sounds more formal than 本. 書籍 is used for books as publications, for example in a shop or catalog. Everyday conversation can still use 本.
